messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation did not significantly change depression ratings compared with placebo in healthy young adults.
Sentence: "Despite significant increases in vitamin D status in the active group, no significant changes were observed in working memory (F = 1.09; p = 0.30), response inhibition (F = 0.82; p = 0.37), cognitive flexibility (F = 1.37; p = 0.24) or secondary outcomes."
Measured as: ratings of depression
Population: Healthy young adults recruited at The University of Queensland
Intervention: Vitamin D 5000 IU cholecalciferol capsule daily for six weeks
Comparator: Identical placebo capsule
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 128
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficient patients scored higher on HADS-D depression than those with insufficient or sufficient vitamin D.
Sentence: "Patients with vitamin D deficiency scored higher on the HADS-D scale and on an anhedonia symptom factor than those with insufficient (p-values ≤ 0.023) or sufficient (p-values ≤ 0.008) vitamin D."
Measured as: HADS-D score
Population: 380 patients hospitalized with an ICD-10 depressive episode
Intervention: Serum 25-OH D level (deficient <50 nmol/l vs insufficient/sufficient), observational
Comparator: Patients with insufficient or sufficient vitamin D
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 380
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A is a placebo-controlled RCT of supplementation in healthy young adults finding no effect, while Study B is a cross-sectional association in hospitalized depressed patients; the populations and designs differ enough that the findings are genuinely in different directions for the question.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population"],"detail":"design: randomized trial of supplementation vs cross-sectional serum association; population: healthy young adults vs 380 hospitalized patients with depressive episode"}
